patients.summary: Office administrator with long-standing constipation and colonic diverticulosis who joined in 2023. In 2025 she had an ED visit for sigmoid diverticulitis and an August admission for necrotizing pancreatitis; in February 2026 she bled from isolated gastric varices due to portal vein thrombosis and is now on apixaban and nadolol under hepatology.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establish care

44 y/o woman, office administrator at a property management firm, transferring after her internist retired. Feels well. Main ongoing issue is constipation going back more than a decade: hard stools every 2-3 days without her regimen, near-daily and soft with it. Takes Miralax 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg twice a day. Every so often sees a streak of bright blood on the paper after a hard stool; none in recent months. That prompted a colonoscopy in 2021 (records reviewed): sigmoid diverticula, no polyps. No abdominal pain, weight stable, no night symptoms.

PMH: chronic constipation; diverticulosis (sigmoid).
PSH: none.
Meds: as above, all OTC.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: mother has diverticulosis; sister had a DVT; father with type 2 diabetes.
SH: never smoked, does not drink, no drug use. Walks at lunch most days.
GYN: periods regular. Pap/HPV 2020 negative. Mammogram 10/2022 normal.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds, no masses or organomegaly. No edema. Skin without rashes. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Chronic constipation — well controlled on current regimen; continue. Fluids, keep up the fiber.
2. Diverticulosis — reviewed; next colonoscopy 2031.
3. Health maintenance — CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (father with T2DM), TSH. One-time HCV and HIV screening, she agrees. Mammogram due 10/2023, order placed. Pap due 2025. Tdap current. Flu and COVID boosters at a nurse visit in October.

Return in a year for a physical, sooner as needed. She has my cell for anything that comes up.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jennifer — all of Tuesday's bloodwork came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver function, cholesterol, sugar (A1c) and thyroid. The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative, and those don't need repeating. The mammogram order is in; radiology scheduling should reach out. Talk soon.

documents.title: Psyllium question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick one — my sister says I shouldn't take the psyllium at the same time as everything else in the morning. Does it matter? I just dump it all together with coffee.

documents.title: RE: Psyllium question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Fiber can slow absorption of some pills, but nothing you take right now is affected, so mixing them is fine. Just make sure there's a full glass of water with the psyllium. If you ever start a prescription, give it a couple of hours' space from the fiber.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST. Indication: LLQ pain, fever. Findings: Segmental wall thickening of the sigmoid colon with adjacent fat stranding centered on an inflamed diverticulum. Scattered uncomplicated diverticula elsewhere in the sigmoid and descending colon. No abscess, no extraluminal gas, no free fluid. Liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys are normal. Portal and splenic veins enhance normally. Appendix normal. Uterus and ovaries unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis. No abscess or perforation. Background colonic diverticulosis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED — record of visit 06/13/2025, forwarded to PCP.

CC: LLQ pain x 2 days.
HPI: 46-year-old woman with known diverticulosis and chronic constipation. Left lower abdominal pain started two days ago, steady and sharp, worse when she moves or walks. Felt feverish at home, has not wanted to eat. Has not traveled, no ill contacts, has never had pain like this before. Reports that she has occasionally passed small amounts of blood with hard stools in the past; none this week. No vomiting, no urinary symptoms.
PMH: diverticulosis, chronic constipation. PSH: none.
Meds: polyethylene glycol 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother diverticulosis; sister DVT; father type 2 DM.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, office administrator.

Triage: T 38.2, BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 18.
Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. Abdomen tender in the left lower quadrant with voluntary guarding; no rebound; bowel sounds present and normal. No CVA tenderness.
Data: WBC 14.0 K/uL, Hgb 13.2, plt 250 K. CRP 25 mg/L (ref <5). BMP and lipase normal. Urine hCG negative. UA unremarkable.
CT A/P with contrast: uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis, no abscess or free air.

ED course: IV fluids and analgesia; pain improved, tolerated PO.
Impression: acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis.
Disposition: home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID x 10 days, clear liquids advancing to low-residue diet for a few days. Return for worsening pain, persistent fever, vomiting or rectal bleeding. Follow up with PCP within one week.

Pain down to maybe 3/10, no fever since Saturday, eating toast and soup. Holding the Miralax and docusate while stools are loose, still taking psyllium. Booked with PCP Wed 6/18.

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED Friday 6/13 with sigmoid diverticulitis on CT (uncomplicated). WBC was 14, CRP 25. Sent home on amoxicillin-clavulanate.

Today day 6 of 10. Feels much better. Mild ache LLQ when she bends, no fever, eating light meals. Stools a bit loose on the antibiotic. No blood.

Exam: afebrile. Abdomen soft, mild LLQ tenderness only, no guarding or rebound. 

A/P: Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis, improving. Finish the course. Resume bowel regimen once stools firm up, constipation is the bigger risk for her long-term. Colonoscopy in 2021 was complete and showed only diverticula; I don't think she needs a repeat now. Video check-in after the course ends. Warning signs reviewed.

reports.text: Gallbladder normal in wall thickness without stones or sludge. No pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct 4 mm. Liver normal in echotexture. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Pancreatic protocol CT, venous phase through the pelvis. Comparison 06/13/2025. The pancreas is enlarged with surrounding inflammatory stranding and fluid. Non-enhancing parenchyma in the body involves less than 30% of the gland. No gas within the pancreatic bed. No organized walled-off collection. Portal, superior mesenteric and splenic veins are patent. Liver, gallbladder and spleen unremarkable. Colonic diverticulosis without inflammation.
reports.conclusion: Acute necrotizing pancreatitis with less than 30% necrosis. No infected necrosis. Patent splanchnic veins.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine. Admitted 08/11/2025, discharged 08/28/2025.

Principal diagnosis: acute necrotizing pancreatitis (sterile).

Presentation: 46F with diverticulosis and constipation, sudden severe epigastric pain radiating to the back beginning the evening of 8/10, with vomiting. Lipase 2,140 U/L. Triglycerides 142. LFTs and calcium normal. RUQ ultrasound: no gallstones, CBD not dilated. Contrast CT on hospital day 3: necrosis of under 30% of the pancreas, no gas, no infected collection; portal and splenic veins patent.

Course: aggressive IV fluids, IV then oral analgesia, antiemetics, NPO then early enteral feeding by mouth once pain allowed. No organ failure, no ICU stay. No antibiotics were indicated. Surgery and interventional radiology reviewed imaging; no drainage or operation needed. Pain settled over the second week; tolerating low-fat solids from 8/25.

Etiology: not established. No alcohol use, no gallstones on ultrasound, normal triglycerides and calcium, no new medications.

Discharge meds: unchanged home regimen (polyethylene glycol 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg BID).Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; gastroenterology clinic in 6-8 weeks.

events.reason: follow-up after hospital stay for pancreatitis

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Discharge summary reviewed (received 8/29). Admitted 8/11-8/28 with necrotizing pancreatitis, under a third of the gland, sterile, no procedure. No cause found — no alcohol, no stones, TG 142.

Now 6 days home. Eating 5-6 small low-fat meals, mild epigastric soreness after bigger meals, no vomiting, no fever. Down about 4 kg from her usual. Bowels OK on her regimen. Back to work part-time next week.

Exam: thin, comfortable. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no mass, no guarding.

A/P
- Necrotizing pancreatitis, recovering. CBC, CMP, lipase today. Small frequent meals, advance as tolerated. GI follow-up mid-October is booked.
- Chronic constipation: continue regimen.
Call with fever, worsening pain, or vomiting.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw your patient Ms. Esposito in clinic on 10/14/2025, about seven weeks after her admission for sterile necrotizing pancreatitis (necrosis under 30%, no intervention). She has no abdominal pain now, is back to a normal diet including some fat without trouble, and has regained part of the weight she lost. Bowel habit unchanged on her usual regimen. No steatorrhea, no thirst or urinary frequency.

Exam: well, abdomen soft and nontender.

Lipase today normal. A1c 5.4%.

Assessment: recovered from acute necrotizing pancreatitis, cause not identified. Given her full clinical recovery, I have not ordered further imaging; we would scan if pain recurs. I have asked her to avoid alcohol entirely (she does not drink) and to call with recurrent pain.

Medications: polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg twice daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up with us as needed.

Outpatient gastroenterology

Physical, 47F. Big year: ED in June for uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis (resolved on oral antibiotics), then admitted 8/11-8/28 for sterile necrotizing pancreatitis without a cause found. GI saw her 10/14, recovered, A1c 5.4, no further imaging. She feels like herself again. No abdominal pain. Weight holding steady. Bowels regular on regimen. Flu/COVID done 10/9.

Meds: PEG 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg BID. NKDA.
FH unchanged (mother diverticulosis, sister DVT, father T2DM).

Exam: vitals reviewed. NAD. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts without mass. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected. No edema.

A/P
- Preventive: Pap/HPV today. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy next 2031. CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH.
- History of necrotizing pancreatitis: recovered.
- Diverticulosis/constipation: stable.
PHQ-2 1 (a rough summer, mood OK now).

documents.title: Results from your physical

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 11/2024 and 11/2023. Heterogeneously dense breasts. No suspicious findings in either breast. No change from prior.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Return to annual screening.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT abdomen and pelvis, arterial and portal venous phases. Comparison 08/13/2025. Filling defect within the main portal vein consistent with thrombus. Prominent varices in the gastric fundus. Liver smooth in contour with homogeneous enhancement. No ascites. Pancreas without peripancreatic collection. No active contrast extravasation identified. Colonic diverticulosis. No free air.
reports.conclusion: Main portal vein thrombosis, new since 08/2025. Gastric fundal varices. No peripancreatic collection.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, visit 02/13/2026.

Chief complaint: vomiting blood, black stools.
HPI: 47F, history of colonic diverticulosis with an episode of diverticulitis last June, and sterile necrotizing pancreatitis requiring an August admission (managed without surgery). Two days of black tarry stools; this afternoon vomited bright red blood with clots and felt faint standing up. Very tired. No NSAIDs, no alcohol, not on blood thinners.
Meds: polyethylene glycol, psyllium, docusate. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: sister with DVT; mother diverticulosis; father T2DM. SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

Vitals on arrival: BP 98/60, HR 108, RR 16, T 37.1.
Exam: pale, tired-appearing, alert. Abdomen: mild tenderness left upper quadrant, no guarding or rebound. Melena on rectal exam.
Labs: Hgb 7.6, platelets normal, INR 1.1, albumin and bilirubin normal. Lipase normal.
CT A/P: thrombus in the main portal vein, gastric fundal varices.

ED course: two large-bore IVs, 2 units PRBC started, IV pantoprazole, octreotide bolus and infusion, ceftriaxone 1 g IV. GI consulted for urgent endoscopy.
Impression: upper GI bleed, likely variceal, with portal vein thrombosis.
Disposition: admitted to step-down.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 02/13/2026 via the ED; discharged 02/17/2026.

Diagnoses: acute upper GI hemorrhage from isolated gastric (fundal) varices; main portal vein thrombosis, new since 08/2025 imaging. Background: sterile necrotizing pancreatitis 08/2025, colonic diverticulosis, chronic constipation.

Hospital course: Arrived with hematemesis and melena, BP 98/60, HR 108, Hgb 7.6. Received 2 units PRBC, octreotide infusion for 72 hours, IV pantoprazole and ceftriaxone (5 days total, completed in hospital). Upper endoscopy the night of admission: no esophageal varices; isolated varices in the gastric fundus with active bleeding from the fundus; cyanoacrylate injected with hemostasis. No rebleeding thereafter. Hemodynamics normalized by day 2. Diet advanced. Nadolol started once off octreotide. Anticoagulation for the portal vein thrombosis deferred given the fresh variceal bleed; hepatology to decide after repeat endoscopy.

Discharge Hgb 9.4.

Discharge medications:
- NEW nadolol 20 mg daily
- NEW pantoprazole 40 mg daily x 4 weeks
- continue polyethylene glycol 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg BID
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC. Hepatology clinic with repeat EGD in about 3-4 weeks (scheduled 3/10-3/11). Return for any further black stool, vomiting blood, or dizziness.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. Discharge summary and ED record (both received 2/18) reviewed with her.

Summary: 2/13 hematemesis/melena, Hgb 7.6, 2u PRBC. CT: main portal vein thrombus + fundal gastric varices. EGD: isolated gastric varices bleeding from the fundus, glue injection. Discharged 2/17 on nadolol 20 and pantoprazole 40 x4 wks, Hgb 9.4. Presumed link to the August necrotizing pancreatitis; hepatology to weigh anticoagulation after the repeat scope.

Since home: no black stools since 2/15, no vomiting. Tired, a bit winded on stairs, better each day. Lightheaded once getting up quickly on 2/18. Taking everything as prescribed.

Exam: pale conjunctivae. HR in the 70s on nadolol. Abdomen soft, nontender today.

A/P
- Gastric variceal bleed / portal vein thrombosis: CBC today. Referral to hepatology entered so their scheduling has it; repeat EGD + visit set for 3/10-3/11. No NSAIDs, no aspirin.
- Nadolol: tolerating; rise slowly from sitting.
- Bowel regimen: continue, avoid straining.
Went over bleeding warning signs again — straight to the ED.

documents.title: Hepatology Consultation
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Hepatology consultation, visit 03/11/2026. Thank you for the referral.

Ms. Esposito is 47 and was admitted 2/13-2/17 with bleeding from isolated fundal gastric varices, treated with cyanoacrylate, in the setting of a main portal vein thrombus that was absent on her August 2025 CT during sterile necrotizing pancreatitis. Liver is smooth on imaging with normal synthetic function; no evidence of cirrhosis. The thrombosis is most likely a sequel of the pancreatitis.

Repeat upper endoscopy 03/10/2026: the treated fundal varix is obliterated, with no stigmata of recent bleeding. No esophageal varices.

Thrombophilia evaluation (sent at admission and this month, given her sister's DVT): JAK2 V617F not detected; factor V Leiden and prothrombin G20210A negative; anticardiolipin, beta-2 glycoprotein and lupus anticoagulant negative.

She feels well. No further bleeding. Pantoprazole finishes later this month as planned.

Plan:
1. Portal vein thrombosis: start apixaban 5 mg twice daily today, for at least 6 months; repeat contrast CT at that point to decide on duration.
2. Gastric varices, treated: continue nadolol 20 mg daily.
3. Avoid NSAIDs.
We will see her again in 3 months.

Medications at this visit: apixaban 5 mg BID (new), nadolol 20 mg daily, pantoprazole 40 mg daily (to finish 3/16), polyethylene glycol 17 g daily, psyllium 3.4 g daily, docusate 100 mg BID. Allergies: NKDA.

Outpatient hepatology

Follow-up. Two months on apixaban 5 BID from hepatology, plus nadolol 20 daily; pantoprazole finished in March. No melena, no hematemesis, no gum or nose bleeding, bruises a little more easily. Energy back to normal, working full days. Bowels regular on PEG/psyllium/docusate, not straining.

Exam: color good. Pulse 62, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

- Gastric varices, treated: nadolol, HR at target range per hepatology.
- Constipation: keep stools soft, especially now.
Hepatology next month. Physical in the fall.
